customManagers.description: Homebrew/actions tags have four parts (2026.11.02.1), which the github-actions manager truncates to three and then cannot find, so this manager reads the full tag.

packageRules.description: The Homebrew/actions custom manager above owns these pins; the built-in manager would only raise its truncated-tag warning.

@types/node describes the runtime, so it tracks the oldest Node pi-wt supports (the floor of its engines) rather than the newest DefinitelyTyped release or the Node mise.toml develops on. Types from a later major describe APIs the floor does not have, and tsc believes them. Raise the ceiling when the engines floor moves.

mise lock writes .mise/locks for mise.renovate.lock, and Renovate's mise manager regenerates it when it bumps that file. The npm manager would also bump the sidecar's package.json on its own, out of step with its aube-lock.yaml and the digest in mise.renovate.lock
pi-wt follows Pi releases as they ship, so Pi skips the minimum release age that holds every other dependency
Pi updates raise the devDependency floors so pi-wt is developed against the Pi it tracks. The peerDependencies stay "*" so pi-wt accepts whichever Pi hosts it

Pi's docs/packages.md has a package declare the packages Pi provides as peerDependencies at "*", so it loads in whichever Pi hosts it. Renovate leaves those peers alone; the devDependencies carry the Pi the package is built against.
